messages:
IncidentBot: Pager: Elevated 5xx rate detected for model-runner-us-west-2 pool (current 5xx=18%, baseline 0.9%) — alerting on-call (rule: inference.runtime.5xx.spike). Triggered 2025-02-14T03:05:56Z.

Elle (oncall): Ack — I'm on it. Pulling logs and checking routing.

Sam RTE: Seeing repeated segfaults and OOM traces in model-runner logs for container id 7f3a9c. Sample tail: 
```
[2025-02-14T03:04:03Z] model-runner: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f4a3c... libtorch_cuda.so +0x12f4
[2025-02-14T03:04:03Z] runtime: GPU memory alloc failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2025-02-14T03:04:04Z] process crashed with signal 11
```
Noticing it spikes when batch_size > 16.

Maya (infra): Which driver/kernel combo? Any kernel oops in dmesg?

Sam RTE: dmesg shows repeated GPU driver recoveries: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:03:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, PID=10244, p=0, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568900] pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=0000
```
Also attached short nvidia-smi snapshot: 
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 530.41.01   Driver Version: 530.41.01   CUDA Version: 12.1     |
| GPU 0: A100-40GB       39831MiB / 40536MiB | process: model-runner (PID 10244)
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Memory climbs to full, then OOM / segfault.

Juan (support): Customer impact: 12 customer tickets opened in last 20min, mostly hosted API timeouts/502s. Notifying status page.

Elle (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) Reroute traffic from affected pool to fallback pool (us-west-2-fallback-quant) 2) Drain the 3 nodes showing repeated crashes 3) Patch model runner to cap batch_size=8 and disable continuous batching temporarily. Executing reroute now.

Sam RTE: Running reroute CLI: 
```
$ rcli reroute --from model-runner-us-west-2 --to us-west-2-fallback-quant --weight 1.0 --reason "runtime OOM/segfaults"
Routing change accepted. Starting gradual shift (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
```

Sam RTE: Also applied hotpatch to deployment to set ENV INFER_MAX_BATCH=8 and INFER_BATCHING=false; launching rolling restart of model-runner pods. Patch command: 
```
$ kubectl patch deploy model-runner -n inference --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runner","env":[{"name":"INFER_MAX_BATCH","value":"8"},{"name":"INFER_BATCHING","value":"false"}]}]}}}'
```
Pods are restarting now.

Maya (infra): I'm seeing kernel oops on two nodes referencing nvidia driver 530. I'll coordinate node reboots with safe drain. Starting reboot sequence for nodes: i-0a1b2c3d, i-0d3c2b1a. ETA ~8-12 minutes per node.

Anna (custops): Quick impact summary for ops: Estimated ~7% of total requests in last 30m affected; two enterprise customers saw ~15% failure rate. I've prepped templated customer note and will send once we confirm routing is stable.

Elle (oncall): Confirming: routing at 100% to fallback? Sam?

Sam RTE: Routing reached 100% after 6 minutes; 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 2.1% within 3 minutes. Ongoing node restarts and hotpatching. Error signatures still present on drained nodes but traffic away from them.

Juan (support): Status page updated: "Partial degradation — elevated errors impacting inference in US-WEST-2. Mitigation in progress; see updates."

Maya (infra): Node reboots finished for two nodes; kernel oops persisted on one node after reboot — isolating and will maintain offline. Opening infra ticket to schedule GPU driver rollback to 525.x for that host.

Sam RTE: Action items for next hour: collect full core dumps, run model with smaller micro-batch locally to reproduce, and coordinate with driver team for rollback plan.

Elle (oncall): TL;DR: Cause likely GPU driver/runner interaction causing OOM -> segfault under high batch sizes. Mitigations: reroute to quantized fallback pool, cap batching, drain/reboot problematic nodes, escalate driver rollback. Customer impact: reduced after reroute, support outreach queued. We will keep this thread for RCA write-up. :white_check_mark: 

IncidentBot: Incident status changed to "mitigating" — pager cleared at 2025-02-14T03:44:56Z. Keep monitoring for recurrence.
